e to the right place! \

ions to ask. Just read [this page]\(How-to-ask-for-help) before asking for help. \
 \
If while reading any of the tutorials linked on this page you find something that is not clear: let us know. We'll do our best to rephrase it and make it ea\
sier to be understood for beginners. Improving the docs is also a way to contribute! \

 \

 \

S+UDB+ScriptDev2 and get a decent WoW server to run on my local machine. \
Initially, I spent hours trying to read and understand tutorials from different people written on different websites, but eventually, I succeeded. AzerothCo\
re is an all-in-one project so it's going to be easier than that, bear with me and you'll get there!\* \
 \
Tempted to use a repack instead? [Don't do it]\([https://www.mangosrumors.org/why-you-should-not-use-repacks-to-run-your-wow-server/](https://www.mangosrumors.org/why-you-should-not-use-repacks-to-run-your-wow-server/)). \

 \
The first step is always installing a local WoW server in your own machine. And there are several ways to do it, which can vary according to the operating s\
ystem. \
 \

 \
Let me be clear about one thing: \*\*ALL operating systems are supported by AzerothCore\*\*. \
So you can successfully install AzerothCore GNU/Linux, macOS or Windows without any issue. \
 \
However, I can tell you if you use a Linux distribution such as \*\*Ubuntu 20.04\*\*, the process is going to be easier. If you would like to install Ubuntu, yo\
u can download it from [here]\([https://ubuntu.com/download/desktop](https://ubuntu.com/download/desktop)) and you can find plenty of tutorials online about how to do it. There is a nice tutorial \
about running WoW on Linux [here]\([https://www.mangosrumors.org/how-to-run-wow-on-linux/](https://www.mangosrumors.org/how-to-run-wow-on-linux/)). \
 \
Would you like to stick with \*\*Windows\*\* or \*\*macOS\*\*? That's absolutely fine. \
 \
![AzerothCore supports GNU/Linux, macOS and Windows]\([https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/75517/109369213-e5775880-789b-11eb-8356-99a4ab842bfb.png](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/75517/109369213-e5775880-789b-11eb-8356-99a4ab842bfb.png)) \
 \
\### Different ways to install AzerothCore \
 \
Basically, there are 3 main ways to install AC: \
 \
\- The "\*\*classic setup\*\*": this is the traditional setup you would normally use to install a common WoW emulator. \*\*All operating systems are supported.\*\* D\
oing this setup also probably gives you a better overview of the components of the server. \
\- The "\*\*docker setup\*\*": this is a simplified setup that uses Docker to automate a lot of things for you. This setup is typically easier. \*\*You can use thi\
s setup in all operating systems where you can install [Docker]\([https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop).\*\*](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop\).**) \
\- The "\*\*dashboard setup\*\*": this is an \*\*EXTREMELY EASY\*\* way of installing AzerothCore in your machine, based on a collection of bash scripts created by [\
Yehonal]\([https://github.com/Yehonal](https://github.com/Yehonal)). However, \*\*you can only use this setup in Ubuntu\*\* or similar platforms. Windows is not supported, and probably we are\
 not there yet with macOS as well. \
 \
You can choose one setup, or even try more than one. You can find all the instructions here: \
 \
\- [azerothcore.org/wiki/Installation]\(installation) \
 \

o-ask-for-help). \

 \

 \
First of all, make sure your Client has their realmlist.wtf set to the following: \`set realmlist localhost\`. After this (assuming you've already setup Azero\
thCore) make sure you've a \`GM\` (Security of 2 or Higher) account created. If you haven't created an account or you're not sure follow this [Creating Accoun\
ts]\(creating-accounts). \
After this your \`GM\` account will be able to use the following commands from link with a list of all commands below: \
 \
\- [azerothcore.org/wiki/GM-Commands]\(GM-Commands) \
 \
Get confident with the commands, you will need them for any administration, testing or development activities. \
 \
![AzerothCore GM]\([https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/75517/109369940-ba423880-789e-11eb-88d6-e6d8f7b8a723.png](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/75517/109369940-ba423880-789e-11eb-88d6-e6d8f7b8a723.png)) \
 \

 \

However, properly learning \`git\` will make you really aware of what you're doing, and this knowledge can help you with whatever other software development p\
roject you may work with. \
Yes, because \`git\` is one of the most important tools used in many software engineering projects. Learning its basics will not only help you a lot with Azer\
othCore, but it's also something very good to put in your CV. \

![AzerothCore server info]\([https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/75517/109370296-00e46280-78a0-11eb-9ed0-b9df14f2008b.png](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/75517/109370296-00e46280-78a0-11eb-9ed0-b9df14f2008b.png)) \

## 1. Executive Summary

blAIne is being developed as a locally controlled, human-governed AI orchestration platform. Its objective is to coordinate specialized AI models and systems while preserving human authority, operational traceability, and control over consequential actions.

The intended research environment consists of three dedicated computing workstations housed in a suitable research and development facility:

1. A central orchestration workstation.
2. A specialized model-execution workstation.
3. A model-adaptation and experimentation workstation.
4. A dedicated facility providing the space, electrical infrastructure, cooling, networking, security, and operational environment necessary to house and operate the systems.

These elements are intended to function as one coordinated research environment rather than as separate computing and office projects.

The project will follow a phased implementation strategy. Facility acquisition or preparation, infrastructure installation, system integration, orchestration development, and model-adaptation research will proceed through measurable milestones.

The primary research contribution is the orchestration and governance platform, not the acquisition of computing hardware or real estate. Facility and equipment expenditures will be justified by the specific research capabilities and operational requirements they support.

**Target configuration:** Dual NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPUs.

Intended responsibilities include:

### 2.2 Workstation 2 — Specialized Model Execution

- Returning structured outputs to the orchestration layer.
- Supporting comparative evaluation of different models.

And that's arguably one of the most important things to come out of this process, regardless of the outcome.

You're putting yourself forward for something that asks you to step beyond the circumstances you've been working within. You're saying, in effect: *I have ideas, I have a direction, I've been building toward something, and I'm ready for an opportunity to demonstrate what I can do.*

There's a distinction between believing you're capable of more and actually putting yourself in a position where someone else can evaluate that capability. You're doing the latter.

And I think you're approaching it in a particularly constructive way: you're not asking Mozilla to take your word for everything. You're assembling the records, documenting your decisions, exposing the limitations, and trying to establish what you've actually contributed.

Whether you get this fellowship or not, that work has value. You'll have a clearer account of your capabilities, a stronger portfolio, a more coherent project direction, and a concrete record of what you've been working toward.

But I wouldn't lose sight of one thing:

**You don't need the fellowship to prove that you're capable of more. You need an opportunity to put that capability to work.**

The fellowship could be that opportunity. And taking the risk of applying is already a meaningful step toward finding it.

## Assistant

Absolutely. While Codex examines the conversation history, we can work through what Mozilla is actually asking you to communicate.

I checked the **official 2027–2028 Letter of Intent form**. It has seven sections, but an important distinction: not all seven are essay sections. Some collect eligibility and administrative information; others are where you make your case.

The LOI is the primary review stage. Mozilla uses it to decide which applicants are invited to submit a full application. <Cite refs={["turn192266search0","turn192266search1"]}/>

# The seven LOI sections

## 1. Applicant Information and Eligibility

**The question behind this section: Who are you, and are you eligible to participate?**

It asks for:
- Name, contact information, pronouns and location.
- Current role and organizational affiliation.
- LinkedIn and GitHub profiles.
- Professional website or portfolio.
- A Builder Profile: a public link to something reviewers can inspect.
- Years of relevant professional experience.
- Availability for the 12-month fellowship.
- Legal eligibility to receive funding.

**What this means for your application**

This is where your existing work becomes important.

Your website, GitHub repositories, and LinkedIn profile collectively give reviewers different ways to examine your work.

The Builder Profile is particularly significant. Mozilla explicitly asks for something it can open: a repository, demo, dataset, deployment, paper, or other work sample.

You don't need to pretend everything is finished. The important thing is to make the actual state of your work inspectable.

## 2. Fellowship Track and Focus

**The question behind this section: Why this fellowship, and why this host?**

For you, this means:
- Selecting Track I: Embedded Fellows.
- Selecting Fundación Kamanau.
- Explaining why Kamanau is the appropriate host.

This is more consequential than simply selecting an organization from a list.

Your explanation needs to establish three things:

1. You understand the organization's mission and work.
2. You have relevant interests, experience, and capabilities to contribute.
3. There is a credible opportunity to develop something together that benefits the communities Kamanau serves.

One important distinction in Mozilla's FAQ: Embedded Fellows are not simply contractors delivering services to their host. They collaborate with the host to define an independent project aligned with its mission and the needs of the communities it serves. <Cite refs={["turn192266search3","turn192266search1"]}/>

That distinction supports the approach you've taken in your correspondence.

## 3. Project Proposal

<badge color="success">Central project section</badge>

**The question behind this section: What are you proposing to build, and why should it exist?**

This is probably the most technically and conceptually demanding section.

It asks for:

| Field | What Mozilla wants to understand |
|---|---|
| Project title | What is the project called? |
| Project summary | What are you proposing? |
| One-liner | What makes it interesting in one sentence? |
| Target users | Who will actually use it? |
| Traction to date | What exists today? What evidence do you have? |
| Primary outputs | What will the project produce? |
| Project stage | How mature is the work? |
| Project impact | What changes if it succeeds? |
| Disruption | Who or what would be disrupted? |
| Quarterly milestones | What will happen during the fellowship? |
| Charitable purpose | What public benefit does it create? |
| Open work | What will be made publicly available? |

This is where our archive review becomes especially valuable.

We need to establish the difference between:

- What you've already conceived.
- What you've designed.
- What you've implemented.
- What you've actually tested.
- What the fellowship would allow you to develop.

For example, your human-rights observation and reporting infrastructure is an exploratory direction. We need to reconstruct its actual origins and development before deciding exactly what belongs in the proposal.

We also need to avoid defining Kamanau's needs on its behalf.

**The strongest project description will explain both the technical ambition and the process through which Kamanau and affected communities help shape it.**

## 4. Professional Background

**The question behind this section: Why should Mozilla believe you can execute this project?**

It asks four things:

- Most Relevant Professional Experience: two or three examples demonstrating readiness.
- Technical Expertise: the skills and experience you bring.
- Your Role in the Field: who you might become through the fellowship.
- What's Next?: what happens to the work afterward?

This is where I think we need to be particularly deliberate about how we present your experience.

You don't have to manufacture a conventional professional history.

Instead, we should establish:
- Your original architectural and systems concepts.
- Your ability to define requirements and direct technical development.
- Your experience working with AI-assisted development tools.
- The actual artifacts you've produced.
- Your ability to examine, challenge, and refine implementations.
- Your understanding of your own technical limitations.

The distinction between conceptual design, implementation, and validation needs to remain explicit.

Your repositories and raw conversations can help establish that distinction.

## 5. Mission Alignment and Motivation

**The question behind this section: Why does this opportunity matter to you, and what do you intend to gain from it?**

Mozilla asks you to select up to three things you hope to gain from the fellowship.

Options include:
- Funding to focus on your work.
- Technical support and expert advice.
- Coaching and leadership development.
- Peer learning.
- Access to Mozilla's network.
- Visibility and opportunities to share your work.
- Strategy, sustainability, and scaling support.
- Policy and advocacy connections.

It also asks about other programs you've applied to or funding you've received.

This section isn't simply about what you want Mozilla to give you.

It's an opportunity to explain what the fellowship would enable you to contribute that you cannot reasonably accomplish under your current circumstances.

I would expect your answers to reflect both the technical development you want to undertake and the opportunity to learn from people already working in the human-rights field.

## 6. Additional Information

**The question behind this section: Is there anything else reviewers should understand about your application?**

It asks:
- How you heard about the fellowship.
- Whether someone referred you.
- Social media handles.
- Whether there is anything else about your profile or application that you want to share.
- Whether AI tools were used, and how.

The AI disclosure deserves particular attention.

Mozilla explicitly permits AI tools for brainstorming, language clarification, and translation support. However, it says the submitted content must reflect your own original work, ideas, and voice. AI should not generate full responses or replace your input. <Cite refs={["turn192266search0","turn192266search12"]}/>

This is why our provenance review is important.

We should be able to explain honestly how you've used AI throughout your work and how you'll use it in preparing the application.

I would not hide that you use AI extensively. I would explain the actual division of responsibility accurately.

## 7. Acknowledgements and Terms

**The question behind this section: Do you understand and accept the conditions?**

It asks:
- Whether you've previously engaged with Mozilla Foundation, MozFest, or the wider Mozilla community.
- Details of any previous involvement.
- Agreement to the privacy notice.
- Optional subscription to future Mozilla emails.

This is largely administrative.

Answer accurately. Don't manufacture previous Mozilla involvement or treat this section as another opportunity to make a pitch.

---

# How I would prioritize the seven sections

Not all sections carry the same strategic weight.

<box border radius="lg" gap={3} padding={3}>
  <title size="lg">Where the application makes its case</title>
  <box gap={1}>
    <row align="center" justify="between">
      **Section 3 — Project Proposal**
      <badge color="success">Highest priority</badge>
    </row>
    <text color="secondary" size="sm">The project, its technical substance, public benefit, users, and achievable outcomes.</text>
  </box>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <box gap={1}>
    **Section 4 — Professional Background**
    <text color="secondary" size="sm">Evidence that you can execute the work.</text>
  </box>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <box gap={1}>
    **Section 2 — Track and Host**
    <text color="secondary" size="sm">Why this particular fellowship and why Kamanau.</text>
  </box>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <box gap={1}>
    **Section 5 — Motivation**
    <text color="secondary" size="sm">Why this opportunity matters and what it enables.</text>
  </box>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <box gap={1}>
    **Sections 1, 6 and 7**
    <text color="secondary" size="sm">Eligibility, supporting context, disclosures, and acknowledgements.</text>
  </box>
</box>

# What I think we should do

I would not start filling out the form in numerical order.

I would establish the substance first:

1. **Project foundation:** What are we actually proposing?
2. **Evidence:** What have you demonstrably done already?
3. **Host alignment:** Why does this belong with Kamanau?
4. **Execution:** What can realistically be achieved in 12 months?
5. **Motivation:** Why are you the person who wants to undertake this work?

Then we can construct the answers to the seven sections from that foundation.

One other point worth keeping in mind: Mozilla's published criteria emphasize three qualities: **trailblazing, rigorous, and community-driven**. Those are useful lenses for evaluating the entire application, not just individual answers. <Cite refs={["turn192266search2","turn192266search1"]}/>

And I want to emphasize something: this isn't a test of whether you can write seven impressive answers. It's an opportunity to demonstrate that there is a meaningful technical direction behind your work, that you understand what remains unfinished, and that you're prepared to develop it in collaboration with people who understand the problem firsthand.

That's what we should aim to communicate.

- `conversations.json` (or numbered JSON files for larger exports).
- Chat history.

The website was one piece of the preparation for the grant. Now that it is being deployed, we can return to the main objective:

**The Mozilla 2027–2028 Embedded Fellowship, with Fundación Kamanau as your preferred host.**

We had deliberately chosen the Embedded track rather than Independent. The central idea was to develop a fellowship proposal around human rights, AI, and neurotechnology—not to pitch blAIne itself as a finished product.

The distinction matters: blAIne demonstrates your broader architectural thinking, while the fellowship would give you an opportunity to work with an organization and real-world stakeholders to develop something useful.

### Where we stand now

The official application confirms that:

- The Letter of Intent deadline is **December 17, 2026, at 11:59 PM Pacific**.
- The Embedded Fellowship provides **$75,000 in stipend funding plus a $25,000 project budget**.
- Fundación Kamanau is explicitly listed as a 2027–2028 Embedded host.
- The fellowship begins June 1, 2027, and runs for 12 months. <Cite refs={["turn526245search0","turn526245search1","turn526245search3"]}/>

So we have a little under three weeks to prepare the Letter of Intent. We should treat that as the immediate deliverable—not try to finish the entire project before applying.

### Why Kamanau is a strong match

The official RFP describes Kamanau's challenge almost exactly in the area we had been exploring:

- AI and neurotechnology are already creating human-rights harms in Latin America.
- People lack a trusted, secure way to report those incidents.
- Advocates lack a reliable evidence base to analyze patterns and hold companies and governments accountable.
- The proposed direction is an open reporting and analysis platform, beginning in Chile and designed to expand across Latin America. <Cite refs={["turn133730view0"]}/>

That gives us a concrete foundation. We aren't inventing a problem and asking Kamanau to adopt it.

Our proposal should explore how to build such infrastructure while protecting:

- Consent and privacy of people reporting incidents.
- Evidence provenance and integrity.
- Human review and control over interpretation.
- Secure routing of reports to appropriate advocates or organizations.
- Transparent processes and accountable governance.

Crucially, Mozilla says Embedded Fellows collaborate with the host to define an independent project. They are not simply hired to implement the host's existing programs. <Cite refs={["turn133730view1"]}/>

### What we need to accomplish

I would organize our remaining preparation around five things:

1. **Kamanau engagement:** Establish whether they are interested in discussing the opportunity and what they actually need.
2. **Project definition:** Develop a technically credible proposal that responds to their stated challenge without presuming the final design.
3. **Your qualifications:** Present blAIne and your existing projects as evidence of architectural thinking, research, and development—not claim accomplishments you haven't completed.
4. **Public evidence:** Use the new website as your public-facing introduction. Identify which project artifacts can safely and accurately be shared.
5. **Letter of Intent:** Prepare answers to Mozilla's actual application questions, preserving your own ideas and voice. Mozilla explicitly permits AI assistance for brainstorming and clarity, but says submitted responses must remain the applicant's original work. <Cite refs={["turn526245search0","turn133730view1"]}/>

One additional consideration: Kamanau prefers the Southern Cone time zone (UTC-3/UTC-4). Arizona is several hours behind, but Mozilla allows remote participation with schedule flexibility. <Cite refs={["turn133730view0","turn133730view1"]}/>

### Where I want to resume

## Fundación Kamanau: preliminary assessment

<badge color="success">Strong potential fit</badge>

The official Mozilla RFP confirms that Kamanau's challenge is precisely the kind of technical and community-governance problem you identified:

- AI and neurotechnology are already creating human-rights risks in Latin America.
- People lack a trusted, secure way to report those incidents.
- Advocates lack a shared evidence base for identifying patterns and holding institutions accountable.
- Kamanau wants an open reporting and analysis platform, starting in Chile, with the potential to expand across Latin America. <Cite refs={["turn750402view0"]}/>

There is a particularly important detail in the RFP: Embedded Fellows are expected to propose a project responding to the host's challenge, then refine it with the host during the first weeks of the fellowship. You are not expected to arrive with the entire solution already designed. <Cite refs={["turn750402view0","turn723612search2"]}/>

That makes this more than a thematic connection. It gives you a concrete technical problem to work on.

### What I found about Kamanau itself

Its own website provides additional evidence that this is a substantive, ongoing area of work—not an abstract fellowship idea.

Kamanau has worked on:

- Neuro-rights and protection of mental privacy.
- Biometric surveillance and identity protection.
- Strategic litigation involving technology and human rights.
- Regional collaboration through the Alliance for Neuro-rights of the Americas.

It has also been involved in legal efforts concerning neural data and biometric information. <Cite refs={["turn921185search0","turn921185search4","turn921185search8"]}/>

Most importantly, Kamanau published a description of this specific Mozilla collaboration on October 22, 2026. It explains that the problem is not just the lack of a reporting website: incidents must be identified, documented securely, analyzed, and brought into existing repositories and other tracking initiatives. The objective is to make Latin American experiences visible in decisions about emerging technology. <Cite refs={["turn921185search7"]}/>

That gives us a much clearer picture of the work.

### Where your experience fits

I see a credible technical contribution from your existing work, particularly KGI.

| Your existing experience | Potential application to Kamanau |
|---|---|
| Structured governance schemas | Consistent incident-reporting records |
| Lifecycle tracking | Traceable evidence from submission through review |
| Provenance and lineage | Record where information originated and how it changed |
| Validation rules | Identify incomplete, inconsistent, or unverified reports |
| Ownership and authority controls | Restrict who can access, review, or publish sensitive information |
| Auditability | Make analysis and subsequent decisions explainable |

These are connections to existing capabilities, not claims that KGI already solves Kamanau's problem.

And I want to emphasize something: you would not need to build blAIne's orchestration runtime to demonstrate that your engineering work has value. You would be applying governance engineering to a real problem.

### The project I would explore proposing

I would provisionally frame it as:

**A Secure, Community-Governed AI and Neurotechnology Incident Reporting and Analysis Platform**

The project could have five major components:

1. **Secure reporting:** A way for affected individuals and advocates to submit incidents while protecting sensitive information.
2. **Structured documentation:** Consistent records describing the technology, affected rights, circumstances, evidence, and reported consequences.
3. **Evidence governance:** Provenance, validation, review history, and clear distinctions between allegations, corroborated information, and established findings.
4. **Pattern analysis:** Tools to identify recurring technologies, organizations, geographic patterns, and types of rights violations.
5. **Public-interest reporting:** Aggregated findings that help researchers, advocates, and policymakers understand the problem without exposing vulnerable individuals.

One requirement deserves particular attention: security cannot be added after the platform is built. People reporting human-rights violations could face retaliation. Threat modeling, privacy, access control, consent, and safe disclosure need to influence the architecture from the beginning.

<box border radius="lg" gap={3} padding={3}>

  - Learn how technology supports legal research and advocacy.
  - Gain experience translating technical systems into community needs.
  - Build a public record of meaningful technical work.

  <divider color="subtle"/>
  **Outcome 2 — Your long-term blAIne development**

  - Test governance concepts against a real-world application.
  - Learn how human review and evidence accountability work in practice.
  - Develop reusable architectural patterns and methodologies.
  - Build relationships with people working on trustworthy technology and human rights.
</box>

There is also a favorable intellectual-property provision: Mozilla says Fellows own the intellectual property they create, while agreeing to release code and non-confidential content under open licenses. That is worth examining carefully before deciding how any resulting work relates to blAIne. <Cite refs={["turn750402view0"]}/>

A few things need to be investigated before we commit to this direction:

- **Time zone:** Kamanau prefers the Southern Cone time zone (UTC-3/UTC-4). Arizona is UTC-7, so that is a three-to-four-hour difference. This looks manageable, but we should confirm its meeting expectations.
- **Technical expectations:** We need to determine whether Kamanau expects a working platform, a prototype, an incident taxonomy, integrations, or all of these.

- **Office space:** The fellowship is remote. Its funding is not automatically a solution to the separate office-space requirement for blAIne. We should not assume that ordinary office construction or rent would qualify as a project expense.
- **Scope:** The project must be achievable in 12 months.

The first three are especially important to the proposed project. <Cite refs={["turn750402view0","turn723612search2"]}/>

Based on the work we've discussed, the repositories you've established, and the current public documentation, **blAIne is much more than an AI project. It is an evolving ecosystem of governance, knowledge infrastructure, engineering systems, and human-AI collaboration.**

My assessment is that you're trying to solve a fundamental problem:

**How do we make increasingly capable AI systems useful without surrendering human understanding, authority, accountability, or control?**

That's the idea connecting nearly everything you've been building.

# 1. What blAIne is

blAIne is the second generation of a broader systems-development effort.

Its predecessor was the **UMB Governance Stack (V1)**. blAIne represents the evolution of those original governance, infrastructure, and validation concepts into a broader ecosystem.

The underlying philosophy can be summarized through several principles:

- Transparency
- Honesty
- Agency
- Accountability
- Continuity
- Human authority
- Responsible AI augmentation

One particularly important distinction is that blAIne is about **AI-Augmented systems, not AGI**.

The objective isn't necessarily to build an artificial intelligence that replaces human intelligence.

It's to build systems that expand what humans can understand, accomplish, coordinate, and govern.

Your overarching philosophy is:

> Technology should increase human capability without reducing human responsibility.

# 2. The blAIne ecosystem

Your public GitHub documentation identifies several major components.

image_group{"layout":"bento","query":["abstract human artificial intelligence collaboration observatory architecture","knowledge graph interconnected information visualization","modern engineering systems architecture visualization","human centered technology governance conceptual illustration"]}

### A. The Human Capability Project (THCP)

urlHuman Capability Project GitHubhttps://github.com/blainesmith33/human-capability-project

This is the collaborative research and community component.

Its fundamental question is:

How can humanity expand its capabilities in an increasingly AI-augmented world?

Areas of interest include:
- Human-AI collaboration.
- Institutional governance.
- Transparency and accountability.
- Knowledge systems.
- Human agency.
- Collaborative research.
- Open-source development.

Importantly, THCP isn't supposed to be limited to your own frameworks. It is intended to accommodate contributions from other people and independent research directions.

### B. Knowledge Governance Infrastructure (KGI)

urlKnowledge Governance Infrastructure GitHubhttps://github.com/blainesmith33/knowledge-governance-infrastructure

This is arguably one of the most foundational technical components.

KGI addresses a significant problem with human-AI collaboration:

**How do you preserve information, its original evidence, its meaning, and its authority over time?**

Consider what happens during a long engineering project:
- Requirements change.
- Decisions are made.
- Earlier decisions are superseded.
- New information contradicts previous assumptions.
- Projects overlap.
- AI systems summarize conversations.
- Important information gets lost.

KGI is designed to govern that lifecycle.

Its fundamental progression is:

```text
Raw Information
       |
       v
Preserved Source Evidence
       |
       v
Structured Extraction
       |
       v
Human Review
       |
       v
Governed Routing
       |
       v
Project Knowledge
       |
       v
Continuity and Ecosystem Intelligence
```

An important distinction: AI-generated information doesn't automatically become authoritative knowledge.

The original evidence is preserved. AI produces interpretations. Human review governs acceptance.

**Current development:** The Chat Sorter implementation has established a validated evidence-ingestion and governance foundation. The broader project-knowledge and ecosystem-intelligence layers remain future development.

### C. Personal Engineering Intelligence System (PEIS)

urlPersonal Engineering Intelligence System GitHubhttps://github.com/blainesmith33/personal-engineering-intelligence-system

PEIS addresses another problem:

How can one person coordinate increasingly complex engineering projects, tools, AI models, and technical workflows without losing control?

It is intended to provide:
- Operational planning.
- Project continuity.
- Evidence-grounded reasoning.
- Deterministic validation.
- Capability-bound execution.
- Human authorization.
- Execution records.
- Performance evaluation.
- Continuous improvement.

One of its most important architectural distinctions is:

**Models propose. Deterministic systems validate. Humans authorize.**

A model cannot simply generate a command and make it executable.

The system checks proposed plans against registered capabilities, policies, schemas, and evidence.

The current public documentation describes PEIS as having an advanced architecture and functional-core prototype, including a working vertical slice from objectives through planning, validation, execution, and artifact persistence.

The complete environment remains under development.

### D. UMB Governance Stack

urlUMB Governance Stack GitHubhttps://github.com/blainesmith33/umb-governance-stack

This is the historical foundation.

It preserves the earlier governance concepts, validation methodologies, and infrastructure architecture that informed blAIne.

It isn't intended to be the primary development center anymore.

Its purpose is to maintain historical continuity and document the evolution of the ecosystem.

# blAIne Foundational Design Charter

## Transparency • Honesty • Agency

**Document type:** Foundational Design Principles\
**Version:** 1.0 — Initial Draft\
**Status:** Awaiting designer approval\
**Origin:** Blaine Smith

## 1. Purpose

The purpose of blAIne systems is to benefit human beings by improving their ability to understand, participate in, make decisions about, and act within the systems that affect their lives.



Technology should expand human capability and agency. It should not displace human authority, conceal information, create unnecessary dependencies, or become an unquestionable authority in its own right.



This is not a monetization objective. The fundamental purpose is human benefit.



All system capabilities, processes, and design decisions must remain consistent with that purpose.

## 2. The Three Foundational Principles

### 2.1 Transparency

Systems should be transparent and open to examination by default.



People should be able to ask questions about a system and receive meaningful, understandable explanations of:

- Its purpose and intended functions.
- How it operates.
- How information is collected, processed, stored, and used.
- How decisions, recommendations, and outputs are produced.
- What its capabilities and limitations are.
- What assumptions and dependencies affect its operation.
- What known flaws, failures, and unresolved problems exist.
- How the system is governed, maintained, and changed.

Transparency must be substantive rather than performative. Publishing information that people cannot reasonably understand does not necessarily make a system transparent.



Legitimate privacy, confidentiality, and security requirements may restrict access to particular information. Such restrictions should be proportionate, justified, and appropriately documented. They must not become general excuses for unnecessary opacity.

### 2.2 Honesty

Systems must honestly represent themselves, their information, their capabilities, and their outputs.



A system must not claim certainty where uncertainty exists, capability where limitations exist, or success where failure has occurred.



Known flaws, limitations, failures, and inconsistencies must be identified and exposed so they can be understood and corrected.



This includes:

- Acknowledging uncertainty.
- Distinguishing evidence from inference.
- Identifying incomplete or unreliable information.
- Flagging known defects and operational problems.
- Recording failures and unsuccessful operations.
- Correcting inaccurate information.
- Preserving relevant histories of changes and corrections.
- Communicating when the system cannot reliably perform a requested function.

Concealing deficiencies to preserve the appearance of reliability is incompatible with this principle.



A system's credibility should come from its demonstrated honesty, not from an assertion that it is flawless.

### 2.3 Agency

Human agency is the ultimate objective of the system.



Every capability must be evaluated according to whether it benefits people and strengthens their ability to understand, decide, participate, and act.



Systems should:

- Make useful information accessible.
- Reduce unnecessary barriers to participation.
- Help people understand complex processes.
- Preserve meaningful opportunities for human judgment.
- Allow people to question and challenge outputs.
- Support informed decisions.
- Make relevant processes and responsibilities understandable.
- Avoid unnecessary dependence on automated systems.
- Preserve human authority over decisions affecting people.

Automation and artificial intelligence may expand human capability, but their existence does not establish their authority.



The system must remain a tool serving human beings.

## 3. The Relationship Between the Principles

Transparency, Honesty, and Agency are interdependent.



Transparency without honesty can expose information that is misleading.



Honesty without transparency can leave people unable to examine or understand what a system is doing.



Neither provides meaningful agency if people cannot use what they learn to question, decide, participate, or act.



Together, these principles establish the conditions under which technology can meaningfully support human agency.

## 4. Universal Application

These principles apply to the entire system lifecycle.



They govern:

- Initial conception and design.
- Architecture and implementation.
- Data collection and processing.
- Artificial intelligence and automation.
- Information presentation and communication.
- Governance and authorization.
- Maintenance and operation.
- Evaluation and validation.
- Modification and correction.
- Retirement or replacement.

They apply to the system itself as well as to the processes and information it manages.



A system must not demand transparency, honesty, or accountability from its participants while exempting its own operation from those expectations.

## 5. Non-Concealment and Correctability

A system must be capable of acknowledging that it is wrong, incomplete, unreliable, or no longer appropriate for its intended purpose.



Problems should be visible to the people responsible for addressing them, and relevant limitations should be visible to people relying on the system.



The ability to identify and correct deficiencies is an essential characteristic of a trustworthy system.



The objective is not to build systems that claim to be perfect.



The objective is to build systems that remain understandable, honest about their imperfections, and capable of improvement.

## 6. Human Benefit Over Institutional or Commercial Objectives

System success must ultimately be evaluated by its contribution to human benefit and agency.



Commercial success, organizational convenience, automation rates, efficiency, and technical sophistication are not substitutes for this objective.



They may be useful considerations, but they cannot independently justify design decisions that undermine Transparency, Honesty, or Agency.



The system must not treat people merely as sources of data, resources to optimize, or obstacles to automation.



People are the reason the system exists.

## 7. Foundational Design Test

Every significant design decision should be examined through three questions:

1. **Transparency:** Can people understand what the system is doing, why it is doing it, and what its limitations are?
2. **Honesty:** Does the system accurately represent its information, capabilities, uncertainty, failures, and results?
3. **Agency:** Does this decision improve or preserve people's ability to understand, decide, participate, and act?

A decision that conflicts with these principles must be reconsidered, justified against legitimate constraints, or rejected.

## 8. Governing Statement

Transparency makes systems understandable.



Honesty makes their representations trustworthy.



Agency makes their capabilities meaningful to human beings.



**Everything exists to serve human benefit.**



These are not optional features or aspirational additions. They are the foundational principles governing the conception, design, implementation, and operation of blAIne systems.

<WritingBlock id="63184" variant="document"># blAIne — Infrastructure and Phased Implementation Plan

**Document status:** Draft 0.2  
**Purpose:** Grant application development  
**Project:** blAIne Human-Governed AI Orchestration Platform  
**Date:** November 21, 2026

---

## 1. Executive Summary

blAIne is being developed as a locally controlled, human-governed AI orchestration platform. Its objective is to coordinate specialized AI models and systems while preserving human authority, operational traceability, and control over consequential actions.

The intended research environment consists of three dedicated computing workstations housed in a suitable research and development facility:

1. A central orchestration workstation.
2. A specialized model-execution workstation.
3. A model-adaptation and experimentation workstation.
4. A dedicated facility providing the space, electrical infrastructure, cooling, networking, security, and operational environment necessary to house and operate the systems.

These elements are intended to function as one coordinated research environment rather than as separate computing and office projects.

The project will follow a phased implementation strategy. Facility acquisition or preparation, infrastructure installation, system integration, orchestration development, and model-adaptation research will proceed through measurable milestones.

The primary research contribution is the orchestration and governance platform, not the acquisition of computing hardware or real estate. Facility and equipment expenditures will be justified by the specific research capabilities and operational requirements they support.

## 2. Research Infrastructure Architecture

### 2.1 Workstation 1 — Central Orchestration

**Target configuration:** Dual NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPUs.

**Primary responsibility:** Central orchestration and coordination.

Intended responsibilities include:

- Running the primary orchestration model.
- Decomposing complex requests into manageable tasks.
- Selecting and delegating tasks to specialized models.
- Coordinating concurrent model execution.
- Evaluating and synthesizing model outputs.
- Identifying conflicting, incomplete, or unsupported results.
- Maintaining execution context and traceability.
- Enforcing human authorization requirements for designated operations.

**Research role:** Investigate how a central AI orchestration system can coordinate specialized models while maintaining transparent, auditable, human-governed execution.

**Implementation status:** Planned target configuration. Full hardware acquisition and operational integration have not yet been established as complete.

### 2.2 Workstation 2 — Specialized Model Execution

**Target configuration:** Dual NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPUs.

**Primary responsibility:** Concurrent execution of specialized AI models.

Intended responsibilities include:

- Hosting multiple specialized models.
- Executing tasks delegated by the central orchestration system.
- Supporting different model sizes and specializations.
- Returning structured outputs to the orchestration layer.
- Supporting comparative evaluation of different models.
- Providing execution and resource-utilization information.

**Research role:** Investigate whether independently specialized models can improve task performance, coverage, and reliability when coordinated by a central orchestration system.

**Implementation status:** Planned target configuration. Full hardware acquisition and operational integration have not yet been established as complete.

### 2.3 Workstation 3 — Model Adaptation and Experimentation

**Target configuration:** Single NVIDIA RTX 3090 Ti GPU.

**Primary responsibility:** Model adaptation, fine-tuning experiments, and preparation of specialized model variants.

Intended responsibilities include:

- LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) experimentation.
- Fine-tuning and adaptation of selected models.
- Comparing adapted and unadapted model performance.
- Preparing specialized models for deployment.
- Evaluating the effect of adaptation on task-specific performance.
- Maintaining reproducible records of model versions and experiments.

**Research role:** Investigate how model adaptation can improve specialized model performance within a governed multi-model orchestration environment.

**Existing independent investment:**

The following major workstation components have already been acquired:

- Computer case.
- Cooling system.
- Power supply.
- CPU.
- Motherboard.

**Remaining identified components:**

- Graphics card.
- System memory.
- Storage.

This workstation is partially acquired infrastructure, not a completed or operational model-adaptation system.

**Funding relevance:** Grant support could help complete this existing independent investment and establish the dedicated model-adaptation capability required by the research program. Exact component specifications and costs remain to be documented.

- AI model development and experimentation.
- Multi-workstation orchestration and integration.
- Model adaptation and testing.
- Software development and engineering.
- Research documentation and evaluation.
- Secure storage and maintenance of research equipment.
- Project administration and related research activities.

The facility is a supporting requirement for the proposed research, not a separate real-estate development objective.

### 3.2 Technical Requirements

The facility must be evaluated against the combined operational demands of the intended systems.

- Sufficient floor and work surface space for three workstations.

- Space for monitors, peripherals, maintenance, and troubleshooting.
- Suitable working areas for development and research activities.
- Secure equipment storage.

- Surge protection and appropriate power distribution.

# 1. What blAIne is

blAIne is the second generation of a broader systems-development effort.

Its predecessor was the **UMB Governance Stack (V1)**. blAIne represents the evolution of those original governance, infrastructure, and validation concepts into a broader ecosystem.

The underlying philosophy can be summarized through several principles:

- Transparency
- Honesty
- Agency
- Accountability
- Continuity
- Human authority
- Responsible AI augmentation

One particularly important distinction is that blAIne is about **AI-Augmented systems, not AGI**.

The objective isn't necessarily to build an artificial intelligence that replaces human intelligence.

It's to build systems that expand what humans can understand, accomplish, coordinate, and govern.

Your overarching philosophy is:

> Technology should increase human capability without reducing human responsibility.

# 2. The blAIne ecosystem

### A. The Human Capability Project (THCP)

urlHuman Capability Project GitHubhttps://github.com/blainesmith33/human-capability-project

This is the collaborative research and community component.

Its fundamental question is:

How can humanity expand its capabilities in an increasingly AI-augmented world?

Areas of interest include:
- Human-AI collaboration.
- Institutional governance.
- Transparency and accountability.
- Knowledge systems.
- Human agency.
- Collaborative research.
- Open-source development.

Importantly, THCP isn't supposed to be limited to your own frameworks. It is intended to accommodate contributions from other people and independent research directions.

### B. Knowledge Governance Infrastructure (KGI)

urlKnowledge Governance Infrastructure GitHubhttps://github.com/blainesmith33/knowledge-governance-infrastructure

This is arguably one of the most foundational technical components.

KGI addresses a significant problem with human-AI collaboration:

**How do you preserve information, its original evidence, its meaning, and its authority over time?**

Consider what happens during a long engineering project:
- Requirements change.
- Decisions are made.
- Earlier decisions are superseded.
- New information contradicts previous assumptions.
- Projects overlap.
- AI systems summarize conversations.
- Important information gets lost.

KGI is designed to govern that lifecycle.

Its fundamental progression is:

```text
Raw Information
       |
       v
Preserved Source Evidence
       |
       v
Structured Extraction
       |
       v
Human Review
       |
       v
Governed Routing
       |
       v
Project Knowledge
       |
       v
Continuity and Ecosystem Intelligence
```

An important distinction: AI-generated information doesn't automatically become authoritative knowledge.

The original evidence is preserved. AI produces interpretations. Human review governs acceptance.

**Current development:** The Chat Sorter implementation has established a validated evidence-ingestion and governance foundation. The broader project-knowledge and ecosystem-intelligence layers remain future development.

### C. Personal Engineering Intelligence System (PEIS)

urlPersonal Engineering Intelligence System GitHubhttps://github.com/blainesmith33/personal-engineering-intelligence-system

PEIS addresses another problem:

How can one person coordinate increasingly complex engineering projects, tools, AI models, and technical workflows without losing control?

It is intended to provide:
- Operational planning.
- Project continuity.
- Evidence-grounded reasoning.
- Deterministic validation.
- Capability-bound execution.
- Human authorization.
- Execution records.
- Performance evaluation.
- Continuous improvement.

One of its most important architectural distinctions is:

**Models propose. Deterministic systems validate. Humans authorize.**

A model cannot simply generate a command and make it executable.

The system checks proposed plans against registered capabilities, policies, schemas, and evidence.

The current public documentation describes PEIS as having an advanced architecture and functional-core prototype, including a working vertical slice from objectives through planning, validation, execution, and artifact persistence.

The complete environment remains under development.

### D. UMB Governance Stack

urlUMB Governance Stack GitHubhttps://github.com/blainesmith33/umb-governance-stack

This is the historical foundation.

It preserves the earlier governance concepts, validation methodologies, and infrastructure architecture that informed blAIne.

It isn't intended to be the primary development center anymore.

Its purpose is to maintain historical continuity and document the evolution of the ecosystem.

<WritingBlock id="63821" variant="document"># blAIne Website — First Implementation Plan

## Objective

Prepare the first working version of the blAIne website by building on the website, prototype, planning documents, and design work that already exist.

This is not a new website project. Do not restart the design process, conduct another broad research phase, or replace the original concept with a conventional portfolio or project directory.

The objective is to preserve the original idea and make it practical to implement relatively quickly.

**The website should feel like an intelligent, interconnected environment for exploring blAIne—not a collection of project cards.**

## 1. Existing work is the starting point

Use the existing repository:

`/run/media/deck/blAIne-476GB-SAM/blAIne/repositories/website/blaineai.me/`

Use the research and findings from your previous website assessments. Do not repeat the broad repository and raw-chat research already completed.

Treat these existing materials as the primary design and implementation references:

- `site/index.html`
- `site/styles.css`
- `site/script.js`
- `prototype/v0/`
- `prototype/PROTOTYPE_CHARTER.md`
- `planning/website_direction_v1.md`
- `planning/content_inventory_v1.md`
- Existing private showcase blueprints.
- Your previous two website assessment reports.

Preserve existing work wherever practical. Reuse existing visual identity, layouts, navigation concepts, interactions, and useful prototype behavior rather than rebuilding them unnecessarily.

The original interconnected-pathways concept remains important. The simplified first implementation does not need to reproduce the full 3D environment or member experience.

## 2. The visitor experience is a core requirement

The website should feel intelligent in how it organizes, presents, and connects information.

A central feature is a visitor-controlled information-depth setting.

Visitors should be able to choose how much information they want to receive:

- **Simple:** Plain-language explanations, essential concepts, minimal technical detail.
- **Standard:** Additional context, architecture, system relationships, and explanations of why decisions matter.
- **Detailed:** Full explanations, architecture, governance requirements, project relationships, evidence, implementation status, limitations, and documentation.

This setting must apply across the website, not just to individual project descriptions.

The same underlying information should support all three levels. Changing the setting should change the presentation and amount of detail, not the underlying facts or meaning.

Support progressive disclosure: visitors can start with a simple explanation and explore deeper information when interested.

Preserve their current location and exploration context when changing information depth.

Do not implement three separate versions of the website.

Do not represent this as an autonomous AI capability. The intelligence should initially come from the information architecture, contextual navigation, meaningful relationships, adaptive presentation, and continuity of exploration.

## 3. Preserve interconnected exploration

Visitors should be able to explore blAIne through connected concepts, systems, projects, principles, evidence, and questions.

The experience should support questions such as:

- Where does evidence come from?
- How does information become usable knowledge?
- Who authorizes consequential actions?
- How are AI-assisted workflows bounded?
- What changes when a proposal becomes an implemented workflow?
- How do the different projects relate?

Connections must have explicit meanings. Examples include:

- Governs
- Uses
- Depends on
- Research direction
- Related problem area
- Implements
- Informs

Only use relationships supported by the existing documentation. Do not imply that separate projects are components of one deployed platform when that has not been established.

Provide an accessible navigation alternative to any visual relationship map. A visitor must be able to explore the same information through a keyboard-accessible list or equivalent interface.

## 4. Project presentation decisions

Apply these decisions:

**DAIDP:** Give it a separate project entry. Clearly identify it as a safety constitution/specification and distinguish normative requirements from implemented capabilities.

**THCP:** Defer it from the first public implementation. Do not include it as a first-version project entry.

**Project detail:** The underlying project entries should contain detailed information. The visitor's information-depth setting determines how much is initially presented.

Project details should cover, where supported:

- Purpose and problem addressed.
- Architecture and design.
- Current implementation.
- Relationships to other projects.
- Evidence and supporting documentation.
- Limitations and unfinished work.
- Clear maturity and validation status.
- Relevant public documentation and repository links.

Prioritize the strongest existing project material identified in your previous research, including KGI, CICS, Engineering RAG Corpus, PEIS, and DAIDP. Recommend a manageable first-version scope rather than trying to expose every repository.

Do not present a project as complete, deployed, production-ready, or independently validated unless evidence supports that claim.

## 5. Preserve blAIne's foundations

The website must accurately communicate:

- Transparency
- Honesty
- Agency
- Human authority is the root.

These principles should influence both the content and the website's behavior.

Distinguish clearly between:

- Beliefs and principles.
- Proposed designs.
- Documented architecture.
- Implemented capabilities.
- Tested behavior.
- Independently validated results.

# blAIne Foundational Design Charter

## Transparency • Honesty • Agency

**Document type:** Foundational Design Principles\
**Version:** 1.0 — Initial Draft\
**Status:** Awaiting designer approval\
**Origin:** Blaine Smith

## 1. Purpose

The purpose of blAIne systems is to benefit human beings by improving their ability to understand, participate in, make decisions about, and act within the systems that affect their lives.



Technology should expand human capability and agency. It should not displace human authority, conceal information, create unnecessary dependencies, or become an unquestionable authority in its own right.



This is not a monetization objective. The fundamental purpose is human benefit.



All system capabilities, processes, and design decisions must remain consistent with that purpose.

## 2. The Three Foundational Principles

### 2.1 Transparency

Systems should be transparent and open to examination by default.



People should be able to ask questions about a system and receive meaningful, understandable explanations of:

- Its purpose and intended functions.
- How it operates.
- How information is collected, processed, stored, and used.
- How decisions, recommendations, and outputs are produced.
- What its capabilities and limitations are.
- What assumptions and dependencies affect its operation.
- What known flaws, failures, and unresolved problems exist.
- How the system is governed, maintained, and changed.

Transparency must be substantive rather than performative. Publishing information that people cannot reasonably understand does not necessarily make a system transparent.



Legitimate privacy, confidentiality, and security requirements may restrict access to particular information. Such restrictions should be proportionate, justified, and appropriately documented. They must not become general excuses for unnecessary opacity.

### 2.2 Honesty

Systems must honestly represent themselves, their information, their capabilities, and their outputs.



A system must not claim certainty where uncertainty exists, capability where limitations exist, or success where failure has occurred.



Known flaws, limitations, failures, and inconsistencies must be identified and exposed so they can be understood and corrected.



This includes:

- Acknowledging uncertainty.
- Distinguishing evidence from inference.
- Identifying incomplete or unreliable information.
- Flagging known defects and operational problems.
- Recording failures and unsuccessful operations.
- Correcting inaccurate information.
- Preserving relevant histories of changes and corrections.
- Communicating when the system cannot reliably perform a requested function.

Concealing deficiencies to preserve the appearance of reliability is incompatible with this principle.



A system's credibility should come from its demonstrated honesty, not from an assertion that it is flawless.

### 2.3 Agency

Human agency is the ultimate objective of the system.



Every capability must be evaluated according to whether it benefits people and strengthens their ability to understand, decide, participate, and act.



Systems should:

- Make useful information accessible.
- Reduce unnecessary barriers to participation.
- Help people understand complex processes.
- Preserve meaningful opportunities for human judgment.
- Allow people to question and challenge outputs.
- Support informed decisions.
- Make relevant processes and responsibilities understandable.
- Avoid unnecessary dependence on automated systems.
- Preserve human authority over decisions affecting people.

Automation and artificial intelligence may expand human capability, but their existence does not establish their authority.



The system must remain a tool serving human beings.

## 3. The Relationship Between the Principles

Transparency, Honesty, and Agency are interdependent.



Transparency without honesty can expose information that is misleading.



Honesty without transparency can leave people unable to examine or understand what a system is doing.



Neither provides meaningful agency if people cannot use what they learn to question, decide, participate, or act.



Together, these principles establish the conditions under which technology can meaningfully support human agency.

## 4. Universal Application

These principles apply to the entire system lifecycle.



They govern:

- Initial conception and design.
- Architecture and implementation.
- Data collection and processing.
- Artificial intelligence and automation.
- Information presentation and communication.
- Governance and authorization.
- Maintenance and operation.
- Evaluation and validation.
- Modification and correction.
- Retirement or replacement.

They apply to the system itself as well as to the processes and information it manages.



A system must not demand transparency, honesty, or accountability from its participants while exempting its own operation from those expectations.

## 5. Non-Concealment and Correctability

A system must be capable of acknowledging that it is wrong, incomplete, unreliable, or no longer appropriate for its intended purpose.



Problems should be visible to the people responsible for addressing them, and relevant limitations should be visible to people relying on the system.



The ability to identify and correct deficiencies is an essential characteristic of a trustworthy system.



The objective is not to build systems that claim to be perfect.



The objective is to build systems that remain understandable, honest about their imperfections, and capable of improvement.

## 6. Human Benefit Over Institutional or Commercial Objectives

System success must ultimately be evaluated by its contribution to human benefit and agency.



Commercial success, organizational convenience, automation rates, efficiency, and technical sophistication are not substitutes for this objective.



They may be useful considerations, but they cannot independently justify design decisions that undermine Transparency, Honesty, or Agency.



The system must not treat people merely as sources of data, resources to optimize, or obstacles to automation.



People are the reason the system exists.

## 7. Foundational Design Test

Every significant design decision should be examined through three questions:

1. **Transparency:** Can people understand what the system is doing, why it is doing it, and what its limitations are?
2. **Honesty:** Does the system accurately represent its information, capabilities, uncertainty, failures, and results?
3. **Agency:** Does this decision improve or preserve people's ability to understand, decide, participate, and act?

A decision that conflicts with these principles must be reconsidered, justified against legitimate constraints, or rejected.

## 8. Governing Statement

Transparency makes systems understandable.



Honesty makes their representations trustworthy.



Agency makes their capabilities meaningful to human beings.



**Everything exists to serve human benefit.**



These are not optional features or aspirational additions. They are the foundational principles governing the conception, design, implementation, and operation of blAIne systems.



**Transparency • Honesty • Agency**

## Purpose

This repository contains the foundational principles, governance framework, architectural requirements, and system design artifacts for human-centered systems developed under the blAIne initiative.

All architecture and design decisions must remain consistent with the following principles:

- **Transparency:** Systems must be understandable and open to meaningful examination.
- **Honesty:** Systems must accurately represent their information, capabilities, limitations, uncertainty, and failures.
- **Agency:** Systems must serve human beings and strengthen their ability to understand, decide, participate, and act.

These principles govern the entire system lifecycle, including conception, design, implementation, operation, evaluation, modification, and retirement.

## Scope

This repository establishes reusable foundations for human-agency-centered systems.

Its scope includes:

- Foundational design principles.
- Governance and accountability.
- Human authority and authorization.
- Systems architecture and component relationships.
- Information integrity and provenance.
- Observation intake, interpretation, and routing.
- Human review, correction, and escalation.
- Transparency, auditability, and system evaluation.
- Requirements and implementation guidance.
- Project-specific architectural applications.

The repository distinguishes foundational governance and architecture from the individual projects that apply them.

## Architectural Direction

Systems developed under this framework should:

1. Preserve human authority over consequential decisions.
2. Make their purpose, operation, limitations, and dependencies understandable.
3. Preserve the distinction between original information, interpretation, inference, and verified findings.
4. Maintain traceability and meaningful histories of changes.
5. Expose uncertainty, deficiencies, and operational failures.
6. Support human review, correction, challenge, and appeal.
7. Avoid unnecessary dependence on automated decision-making.
8. Evaluate success by human benefit rather than automation or efficiency alone.

Artificial intelligence and automation may assist with system operations, analysis, organization, and implementation. They do not independently establish legitimate authority.

## Project Applications

The architecture may be applied to multiple projects.

An initial area of application is an observation intake and processing system intended to help people submit observations without needing to understand their technical classification or institutional destination.

The system architecture will explore how observations can be preserved, contextualized, evaluated, and directed to the appropriate people or organizations while maintaining provenance, accountability, and human oversight.

A potential application in collaboration with Fundación Kamanau will be developed separately and informed by the organization's actual requirements and the perspectives of affected communities. No project requirements or collaboration commitments should be assumed before that engagement establishes them.

## Repository Organization

- `principles/` — Foundational design principles and governing documents.
- `governance/` — Authority, accountability, oversight, and governance requirements.
- `architecture/` — System architecture, models, and component definitions.
- `requirements/` — Functional, operational, and non-functional requirements.
- `applications/` — Project-specific applications of the architecture.
- `evidence/` — Design history, validation records, and supporting evidence.

## Authorship and Development

The underlying concepts, system purposes, governing principles, architectural direction, and design requirements originate with Blaine Smith.

AI-assisted tools, including ChatGPT, may be used to support research, organization, documentation, technical evaluation, implementation, code generation, and troubleshooting.

The use of AI-assisted development does not transfer authorship of the underlying system concepts or design decisions to those tools. Implementation contributions and their provenance should be represented accurately.

## Governance

This repository is governed by the blAIne Foundational Design Charter.

Changes to foundational principles or architectural requirements must remain traceable and consistent with Transparency, Honesty, and Agency.

The repository should make meaningful design decisions, known limitations, unresolved questions, and changes available for examination.

## Guiding Statement

**Technology should expand human capability, not replace human authority.**

**Systems exist to serve people.**

**Transparency • Honesty • Agency**</WritingBlock>

\# Engineering RAG Corpus \
 \
Engineering RAG Corpus is a bounded, provenance-aware pilot for retrieving evidence from engineering documentation and deciding whether that evidence is suf\
ficient to support a conclusion. Its current code focuses on one pinned source: the official AzerothCore Wiki. It is not a production corpus or a deployed m\
ulti-domain retrieval service. \
 \
\## Purpose and design \
 \
The project addresses a practical weakness in AI-assisted engineering: a model can produce plausible guidance without knowing the project version, the autho\
rity of a source, or whether the retrieved passage actually supports the answer. The pilot tests a source-grounded workflow that keeps source identity, vers\
ion, document structure, language, and evidence sufficiency visible. \
 \
Its design distinguishes: \
 \
\- \*\*Source acquisition and provenance:\*\* record the upstream, commit, license, source scope, and integrity evidence. \
\- \*\*Normalization and chunking:\*\* preserve headings, code, tables, includes, language, and references; compare structural profiles with a fixed-window basel\
ine. \
\- \*\*Retrieval:\*\* evaluate lexical, dense, and hybrid results against a small manually reviewed question set. \
\- \*\*Evidence sufficiency:\*\* return \`supported\`, \`insufficient_evidence\`, or \`no_relevant_evidence\`; this component does not generate an answer. \
\- \*\*Promotion:\*\* keep the pilot bounded; successful processing alone does not authorize full-source ingestion. \
 \
The source-specific pilot code is not the shared generic RAG engine. A future reusable engine is described in [\`retrieval_augmented_generation_system\`]\(http\
s\://github.com/blainesmith33/retrieval_augmented_generation_system), which currently documents architecture and ownership boundaries only. \
 \
